title: Benny Carter band: Apollo, Ubangi Club and Depression conditions
summary: They played the Apollo, Ubangi Club and Lafayette; money was thin but everyone loved Carter's writing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did you stay in New York or did you travel at all?
Well we stayed in New York when we worked in New York. Now when we played Philadelphia, Washington, we stayed wherever the engagement was.
But since that was the Depression, it was pretty hard to get that band working I'm told.

Yes, it was, but we seemed to manage somehow. I mean, the money wasn't that great, you know, but it didn't take too much money then to live. And of course everybody just loved working with Benny. On the count, well he made such beautiful charts, everybody loved to play them. See, that's the thing, you'd almost work for Benny Carter for nothing, and go there and play and listen to that good
music. Then to think about the money too much.
What was the audience's reaction to the band usually?

They loved it, they loved it. They loved it. I guess the only reason why Benny wasn't like a Duke Ellington or something like that he was the personality or something, but I don't know you know how they was dealing and wheeling in those days, stealing those managers and things you know. Benny wasn't going for that, you know, and so he made it all right, but he never made it real big.
He was never as much of a showman as Duke.
Lundsford, no, that's right, or Don Redman, or like that you know. Benny Carter was great.
